subject: general
question: Which of the following best describes the style and themes of The Movement poets?

options.text: Very much influenced by the European avant-garde, they were highly experimental and abstract.
The main themes were surrealist images and radical political propaganda.
Their poetry was ironic, nostalgic, and identity-rooted, rejecting often the pretentious elitism.
The poets were completely engrossed in the revival of medieval forms and themes related to religion.

solution:
The correct answer is '**Option 3**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• ***Option 3: Their poetry was ironic, nostalgic, and identity-rooted, rejecting often the pretentious elitism.***

 
 
• **The Movement** was defined by a rejection of the "phoney" or overly obscure. Poets like Philip Larkin and Kingsley Amis favored **clarity** and **rationalism**.
